title: Web scaffolding & import boundaries
subject: main
summary: The web side of the app: the fixed folders of the core and of every slice, how a slice declares its routes and layouts and the core mounts them, and the import boundaries that keep a slice removable.

axioms.text: The [[core]] mounts, owns the [[shell]] and the overlay host, and holds no page, no layout and no application logic.
A [[slice]] declares its pages and how they are mounted, as data; the core mounts what it reads and decides nothing.
A slice can be removed from a product by deleting its folder and fixing the errors.

purpose.intro: The web rules that follow from [[scaffolding-and-import-boundaries|Scaffolding & Import Boundaries]]: where web code lives, how routes and layouts are declared and mounted, and what may import what.

reference.topic: Web: the core and every slice have fixed folders

claims.text: The [[core]] is `apps/main/core/web/src/`: `shells` · `components/sidebar` · `services/api` · `store` · `config` · `routes` · `assets` · `main.tsx` · `env.ts`. It mounts the slices, owns the shells and the routes, and holds no application logic. It has no `shared/`: nothing in the core is shared with a slice, since a slice never imports the core.

`apps/main/slices/shared/web/` holds what the slices share and no slice owns: the screens of the application's edges (`NotFound`, `AccessDenied`, `AppSplashScreen`) and `TitleHeader`, the title band every slice layout puts in `pageHeaderContent`. It is the package `@modules/shared`; the [[core]] and every [[slice]] may import it through `@modules/shared/web`. It imports the repo root's `shared/` only, never the core and never a slice.
A slice's web is `shared/{layouts, components, hooks, helpers}` · `pages/<page>/{<Page>.tsx, components, hooks, helpers}` · `services/{application, api}` · `store` · `routes` · `index.ts`.
Every folder of the shape exists, even when empty: an empty folder holds a `.gitkeep`, and a check script fails when a folder is missing.

`services/api` holds one file per API area, with one client method per endpoint. `services/application` holds the slice's services, one per capability (registration, profile, invitations…), which call `services/api`. Services are singletons.
`store` holds the slice's client state, as a store module; the core's `store` only mounts the store module of every slice.

Generic UI (alert, dialog, empty state, avatar) lives in the repo root's `shared/libs/ui`, not in a slice and not in the core. What a slice owns stays in that slice's `shared/components`, exported by its `web/index.ts` when another slice or the core renders it (user-organization-mgmt's `UserAvatar`, `OrganizationAvatar`, `OrgSwitcher`). Nothing is [[injection|injected]] into a slice to render it: no `useComponents`, no `Default*` fallbacks.

reference.statement: The web side of the app is the [[core]] plus one `web/` per [[slice]]. Each has one shape, and every folder of that shape exists, even when it is empty: a reader never wonders where something would go.

A [[slice]] declares its routes as a tree, as data, and says how each page is mounted: the [[shell]] by name, the slice layout a section's pages share, the pages as its children. The [[core]] iterates the mounted slices and mounts what each declares, under the shell it owns. The core knows no page and no layout of a slice.

claims.text: The route declaration is the one list. A child carries `nav` (its title) when a navigation shows it; the navigation is a projection of that declaration (title, path), never the router's tree. Icons are the navigation's own, a dictionary by path: routing carries no presentation.

Every route node declares `access`: `public`, `signed-in`, or `gated`. After sign-in every page is gated (blocked until the [[unmet-requirements|unmet requirements]] are resolved) unless the node says `signed-in`: accepting an invitation, resolving the requirements themselves. The core maps `access` to the [[shell]] and its guard; a slice never names a shell.

An application layout is structure only, a layout pattern of the library (`@libs/web-layouts`, its compositions), since a slice layout composes it and a slice never imports the core: a composition of the layout primitives with outlets named by the region each one fills (`pageHeaderContent`, `pageLeftSidebarContent`, `mainContainerContent`). It is named by what it is, never by who uses it: `DoubleSidebarLayout` (shell nav, page header, page left sidebar, main), `SingleSidebarLayout` (shell nav, page header, main), `BareLayout` (main only).

A slice layout, in the slice's `shared/layouts`, uses an application layout, fills its outlets with the slice's own components, and gives the main container to its pages through the router outlet. It is the consistency of a section's pages.

The slice layout is a parent route and its pages are its children: a section's chrome stays mounted while its pages change. A page knows no layout; it composes its content with primitives and patterns.

Navigation follows the shared rule: it is owned at the most specific level that covers all its targets. A menu over pages of one [[slice]] belongs to that slice. A menu whose targets span slices belongs to the core — the slices declare their pages, the core assembles.

A section may hold a page of another [[slice]]: the slice that owns the section imports the page through the other slice's `web/index.ts` and places it in its tree. The user settings are user-organization-mgmt's; the notification preferences page is notifications', placed there.
The [[core]] has no page. The destination after sign-in is a core config value, a path, so a product points it where it wants. Tooling pages (the sandbox, the theme editor) are not the core's routes.

reference.statement: The boundaries keep one property: a slice can be removed from a product by deleting its folder and fixing the errors. The errors appear only where the slice was declared to meet the rest: in the [[core]], and in a slice that renders one of its components.

claims.text: The repo root's `shared/` imports nothing from `apps/`, except a config (`shared/configs/`), which may import a [[slice]]'s `shared/index.ts`: the DSL the config is written in (`defineCreditsCatalog`, `defineMessageTypes`). The [[core]], `slices/shared` and every [[slice]] may import from it.
The [[core]] imports a [[slice]] only through its `web/index.ts`.
The [[core]] and every [[slice]] may import `slices/shared` through `@modules/shared/web`. `slices/shared` imports no slice and never the core.
A [[slice]] never imports the [[core]].
A [[slice]] may import another slice's components through that slice's `web/index.ts`: only the ones in its `shared/components`. Never its pages, services, hooks, store, helpers or internal files.

Otherwise slices meet in the [[core]], which places them side by side: the core's `AccountSidebar` renders user-organization-mgmt's `OrgSwitcher` and `UserAvatar` next to notifications' `NotificationBell`, each through its slice's `web/index.ts`.
`pages/<page>/` is private to that page. What two pages need goes in the slice's `shared/`.
Only `services/application` imports `services/api`.
Pages, components and hooks reach logic through `services/application`, never `services/api`.

A component may subscribe to a store directly, through the store's selector hook. It changes state only through the named mutations of the store module that owns the state (`setActiveOrg`), never through raw `getState()` or `setState()`.
A service may read and update state, through the owner's named mutations only.
Helpers import only helpers and `node_modules` packages, never another repo file (components, hooks, pages, services, store, routes).
The core's `services/api` is only the generic client: the 401 and 403 handling. The core holds no application logic.

The boundaries are enforced by `pnpm lint:arch`: the web-boundaries processor, the store control and the folder-shape check. Those between packages (a slice, the core, a library, the repo's `shared/`) are enforced by `pnpm lint:boundaries`.

examples.title: Where slices meet — the account sidebar
examples.text: The sidebar spans slices, so it is the core's. It imports each slice's public surface; neither slice knows the other is there. Removing notifications breaks this file and nothing else.

snippets.caption: apps/main/core/web/src/shared/components/AccountSidebar.tsx
snippets.code:
import { OrgSwitcher } from "@modules/user-organization-mgmt/web";
import { NotificationBell } from "@modules/notifications/web";

examples.title: A slice renders another slice's component
examples.text: A slice may render a component from another slice's `shared/components`, through its `web/index.ts`. Deleting the owning slice breaks exactly these imports.

snippets.caption: allowed
snippets.code: import { OrgSwitcher } from "@modules/user-organization-mgmt/web";   // shared/components, exported by index.ts

snippets.caption: violations
snippets.code:
import { MembershipsPage } from "@modules/user-organization-mgmt/web";              // a page
import { profileService } from "@modules/user-organization-mgmt/web";               // a service
import { OrgSwitcher } from "@modules/user-organization-mgmt/web/shared/components/OrgSwitcher"; // an internal file
